name: Before the Great War — 1910
description: Dated geographic atlas sandbox (1910-01-01). Capitals use geographic coordinates; modern province boundaries are clipped to dated national borders; historical internal divisions are approximate. Colonial control follows an explicit scenario overlay.
worldContext: Start: 1 January 1910. Europe is at peace between its great powers, but alliance commitments, imperial rivalry, naval competition and nationalist disputes create risks. Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy belong to the Triple Alliance; France and Russia are allied, while British understandings with France and Russia are not an automatic obligation to fight every war. The Ottoman state still holds Libya and substantial Balkan territory. Qing rule continues in China. There has been no Italo-Turkish War, Balkan Wars, Sarajevo assassination or world war. Give diplomacy, administrative reform, industrial preparation and domestic opposition time to develop. Do not use tanks, modern aircraft fleets, nuclear weapons or digital communications. Distinguish plans from mobilization, deployment and actual fighting.
simulationRules: Orders are queued immediately and their practical consequences are simulated during time advancement. Do not approve, partially approve or reject orders as a separate process. Explain unfulfilled intentions through events and concrete obstacles. There are no numerical treasury, stability, war-support, political-power or manpower mechanics. Judge capacity qualitatively from history, logistics and elapsed time. Never invent starting tracked formations; create them only from explicit player orders. Map colonies and dependent administrations are not automatically sovereign states. Respect actual diplomatic autonomy. Later historical events are possibilities, never mandatory scripted outcomes. Persisted campaign events and diplomacy override the starting briefing. Include exact geographic event locations when known; use null when uncertain.
